newsitem.title: USA: Florida sheriff stole election, rival charges.
newsitem.headline: Florida sheriff stole election, rival charges.

text.p: Election officials were investigating Thursday whether a Florida sheriff had won his closely contested reelection Nov. 5 by stealing votes.

Civilian employees of the Volusia County Sheriff's Office testified Wednesday that two deputies guarding absentee ballots had said incumbent Sheriff Bob Vogel was "way ahead" before the ballots were even counted.

On election day, challenger Gus Beckstrom appeared to have won the race by more than 4,000 votes. But after absentee ballots were counted, Vogel staged a comeback, retaining his post by nearly 800 votes.

Florida Circuit Court Judge John Doyle seized the ballots and allowed Beckstrom's lawyers to take depositions from witnesses. Beckstrom has called for a new election and his lawyers were examining all 27,310 absentee ballots by hand.
His supporters have also alleged that absentee ballots were filed in the name of dead people and unsolicited ballots were sent to Republicans but not to Democrats. Vogel is a Republican.

The testimony Wednesday disclosed that Vogel had hand-picked two deputies to guard the absentee ballots for four days after they came in. One of the deputies is a former locksmith and the other a lieutenant who had joked that he would be indicted by a grand jury after the election.
Another deputy who worked at the elections office told employees after the election that "We haven't done anything wrong except mark the ballots," according to the testimony.
